posts: "Self-custody wallet Bangladesh" is a real search with a real reason behind it. It also has an answer people don't want: self-custody changes who holds your keys. It does not change what the law where you live permits 🧵

1/ The distinction first. A custodial wallet holds your key — so the exchange can freeze the account, or comply with a court order from its own database. A self-custody wallet generates the key on your device and never sends it anywhere.
2/ That's the whole difference. It says nothing about which chain you're on, which country you're in, or whether the activity itself is permitted. It is purely a statement about where the key lives.

3/ Why the search exists: Bangladesh is one of the world's largest remittance markets, and the 2025 Global Findex still counts it among the eight countries holding more than half of the world's 650M unbanked adults.

4/ And the bank channel is genuinely expensive — globally banks average 9.50% on remittances vs 3.65% for digital providers. Though credit where due: South Asia is the CHEAPEST major destination region at 5.18%, partly from competition on the India/Pakistan/Bangladesh routes.
5/ So the honest framing isn't "Bangladesh is expensive." It's that the bank channel is expensive almost everywhere, and account access is still uneven. That's the structural gap driving the search.

6/ But: Bangladesh Bank has stated repeatedly that trading or transacting in cryptocurrency is not permitted, citing the Foreign Exchange Regulation Act 1947, the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2012 and the Anti-Terrorism Act 2009.

7/ That restriction is on the ACTIVITY, not on a wallet type — so there's no self-custodial carve-out. Holding your own keys doesn't make a restricted transaction permitted, any more than holding cash makes an illegal cash transaction legal.

8/ We're not going to pretend otherwise to sell a wallet. Local law is ours to follow, not to route around. Check Bangladesh Bank's current guidance first; this isn't legal advice. Full post: https://www.swopme.co/blog/self-custody-wallet-bangladesh
